topic.title: Submodular Optimization and Data Selection
topic.overview: Submodular objectives model diminishing returns, making them useful for selecting diverse, representative subsets. These papers study greedy approximations, streaming and dynamic algorithms, nonmonotone objectives, and instance-specific guarantees. Related data-valuation work asks how a score for an item should reflect its contribution to an entire selection sequence.
topic.whyItMatters: The value of an example or resource depends on what has already been chosen. Treating every item independently can waste a budget on redundancy, while worst-case approximation ratios may understate performance on actual instances.
topic.evolution: Early representatives develop incremental and online utility maximization. Later work improves streaming efficiency and extends beyond simple cardinality constraints. Recent studies estimate instance-specific solution quality and connect sequential data selection to utility curvature, using submodular surrogates to make selection scalable and theoretically interpretable.
openQuestions: When does a learned utility retain enough submodular structure for reliable guarantees?
Can instance-specific certificates remain useful as the dataset changes?

papers.title: On Socially Fair Low-Rank Approximation and Column Subset Selection
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditional hardness for fair low-rank approximation while providing faster restricted-setting and polynomial-time bicriteria algorithms.

papers.title: Practical $0.385$-Approximation for Submodular Maximization Subject to a Cardinality Constraint
papers.tldr: A new subset-selection algorithm combines a 0.385 approximation guarantee with practical O(n + k²) query complexity.

papers.title: A Near Linear Query Lower Bound for Submodular Maximization
papers.tldr: Nearly linear query complexity is required for constant-factor submodular maximization, even for value estimation, while additive objectives permit cheaper value estimates.

papers.title: An Asymptotically Optimal Approximation Algorithm for Multiobjective Submodular Maximization at Scale
papers.tldr: A practical algorithm achieves the best-known approximation guarantee for selecting a limited-size set that balances multiple submodular objectives.

papers.title: Breaking Barriers: Combinatorial Algorithms for Non-Monotone Submodular Maximization with Sublinear Adaptivity and $1/e$ Approximation
papers.tldr: Two parallel combinatorial algorithms offer strong approximation guarantees for size-constrained non-monotone submodular maximization, including a ratio approaching 1/e.

papers.title: Discrete and Continuous Difference of Submodular Minimization
papers.tldr: The paper extends difference-of-submodular optimization beyond set functions and develops an algorithm with theoretical guarantees and gains on two integer optimization tasks.

papers.title: Improved Theoretically-Grounded Evolutionary Algorithms for Subset Selection with a Linear Cost Constraint
papers.tldr: A stronger analysis of POMC and the new EPOL algorithm improve guarantees for budget-constrained submodular subset selection.

papers.title: Multinoulli Extension: A Lossless Yet Effective Probabilistic Framework for Subset Selection over Partition Constraints
papers.tldr: Multinoulli-SCG uses a probabilistic relaxation with lossless rounding to reduce evaluations while matching existing subset-selection approximation guarantees.

papers.title: A Unified Approach to Submodular Maximization Under Noise
papers.tldr: A general conversion framework preserves approximation guarantees when suitable submodular optimization algorithms operate with persistent noisy evaluations.

papers.title: Corporate Needs You to Find the Difference: Revisiting Submodular and Supermodular Ratio Optimization Problems
papers.tldr: Several submodular and supermodular optimization problems share an equivalent structure, allowing general algorithms to outperform specialized methods on concrete tasks.

papers.title: GIST: Greedy Independent Set Thresholding for Max-Min Diversification with Submodular Utility
papers.tldr: GIST selects useful, well-separated subsets with a one-half approximation guarantee and strong reported ImageNet sampling results.

papers.title: Monotone and Separable Set Functions: Characterizations and Neural Models
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes vector representations that preserve set containment and develops a stable relaxation for settings where exact preservation is impossible.

papers.title: Non-monotone Submodular Optimization: $p$-Matchoid Constraints and Fully Dynamic Setting
papers.tldr: A dynamic algorithm maintains an approximation-guaranteed solution to non-monotone submodular maximization under p-matchoid constraints as elements are inserted and deleted.

papers.title: Online Two-Stage Submodular Maximization
papers.tldr: The paper introduces online two-stage submodular selection and proves sublinear approximation-aware regret for weighted threshold potential objectives.

papers.title: Streaming Stochastic Submodular Maximization with On-Demand User Requests
papers.tldr: A single-pass streaming algorithm provides guaranteed expected topic coverage under uncertain user visits with memory independent of stream length.

papers.title: A General Framework for Dynamic Consistent Submodular Maximization
papers.tldr: A general framework maintains provably good submodular selections under insertions and deletions while limiting changes to the selected set.

papers.title: HOBIT: Hardness Optimized Batch Sampling for InfoNCE Training
papers.tldr: HOBIT optimizes mini-batch composition to supply informative hard negatives, improving InfoNCE training with negligible reported overhead.

papers.title: Improved Dynamic Algorithm for Non-monotone Submodular Maximization under Cardinality Constraint
papers.tldr: Two dynamic algorithms improve approximation guarantees for cardinality-constrained non-monotone submodular maximization to 0.262 and 0.277.

papers.title: Unifying and Optimizing Data Values for Selection via Sequential Decision-Making
papers.tldr: A sequential-decision view explains limitations of existing data values and motivates scalable, guaranteed greedy data selection.
